title: Parthian Empire
summary: The Parni, a nomadic people from the Central Asian steppe, seized the Seleucid satrapy of Parthia under Arsaces around 247 BCE. Their Arsacid kings went on to rule Iran and Mesopotamia, took tolls on the Silk Road and used mounted archers to defeat Rome, most famously at Carrhae in 53 BCE. Nisa and later Ctesiphon served as capitals. The empire ended in 224 CE, when its Persian vassal Ardashir overthrew the last Arsacid king and founded the Sasanian Empire.

uncertainty.note: Dating traditional start from the Arsacid era beginning around 247 BCE; Livius notes Parni occupation of Astavene in 238 BCE. End is dated to 224 CE when Ardashir I defeated the last Arsacid monarch.

as_recorded.value: The Parthians ruled from 247 BCE to 224 CE

where.modern_name: Old Nisa, Bagyr, near Ashgabat, Turkmenistan (stand-in pin at an early royal capital)

importance.justification: Ruled Iran and Mesopotamia for nearly five centuries and held the Roman advance east at the Euphrates (R3 D3 T3 L3).

related.because: Ardashir I overthrew the last Arsacid monarch in 224 CE to establish the Sasanian Empire.
Ctesiphon on the Tigris served as the winter imperial capital of the Parthian Empire.
Han dynasty embassies under Emperor Wu established formal diplomatic and trade relations with Parthia along the Silk Road.
